9th Degree Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear a ninth chord. Choose its type.
9th Degree Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear a seventh chord with an extra note added. Choose the ninth-chord type that matches the sound.

steps.title: Listen to the whole chord
steps.description: Press Play and listen to the notes together. Notice the overall sound, rather than trying to name every note. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Select Major 9th, Minor 9th, Diminished 7(9), Dominant 9th, Minor 9(♭5) or Dominant 7(♭9). Choose the one that matches what you hear.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

9th Degree Chords · Level 1.about: These chords combine a seventh chord with a ninth. For example, F major seventh uses F, A, C and E. Adding G makes F major ninth. Unlike an add 9 chord, these chords include a seventh as well. Minor 9(♭5) has a lowered fifth; Dominant 7(♭9) has a lowered ninth. The ♭ symbol means that note is one keyboard step lower, counting both white and black keys. This lesson uses chords built on F. The chords start with their root, the note they are named after, at the bottom. Choose only the chord type; there is no separate inversion answer.
9th Degree Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F major ninth: F, A, C and E, with G added above them.
9th Degree Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F major ninth. Choose Major 9th. The same chord type can have its notes arranged differently, so listen to the whole chord.
